Commentary.Commentary: Can't really write a lot about a side which has conceded over 12 per over. All their bowlers were taken to the cleaners. Except for Rabada all went for over 10 per over. Jansen could be happy with the three wickets he got but he too was taken to the cleaners. This is probably not what Markram would have imagined after winning the toss. Now it is onto their batters, if they chase it down, it is going to be the highest chase ever. Can they do it? We will find out.

What carnage! Wow! Brilliant from the Windies. Let me remind you, they lost a wicket in the first over but since then, it has been all about them. It was Kyle Mayers and Johnson Charles who just went after the bowlers right from the word go. The two smashesd the ball all around the park and added 135 in no time. Both crossed half tons. Kyle Mayers fell but Johnson Charles continued.he along with Powell put up another lovely stand. Johnson Charles ended up scoring the fastest ton in this format for his side. Once he fell, it was the Romario Shepherd show and he helped his side cross the 250-run mark.
SIX! BANG! Ends the innings in style! On middle, this is hammered over the mid-wicket fence for a massive biggie. West Indies END WITH 258!

A run feast is what we witnessed in the first T20I where over 200 runs were scored in a rain curtailed game. It was the visitors who came out on top courtesy some power hitting by Powell. It is now time for the second game and the away side now have a chance to seal the series. South Africa on the other hand will be eager to level the series. All to play for, will we have a decider?
... MATCH DAY ...

Well, well, well! The Proteas do not have much time to lick their wounds. In less than 24 hours, South Africa and West Indies will battle it out in the second T20I match of the series. The first match got off to a delayed start and got reduced to a 11-overs match. That meant fireworks apleanty and boy, there was no shortage of entertainment. The hosts put up a commanding total on the board after being put to bat, but the experience of some West Indies players in the T10 helped them to chase down the target. Nevertheless, the Proteas' bowlers gave a run for their money. South Africa have an incredible depth with the blade and will be hoping to showcase their power-hitting ability this time around. David Miller seems to be in his prime. His contribution at the lower-order is quite crucial. West Indies have ample game-chanding players in their ranks themselves. Powell though is certainly leading by example and would hope his players can seal the deal this time around. So, will West Indies be able to run away wih the series? Or will South Africa take it down to the final match? We shall find out together.
